title: Dove's eye
subtitle: A looped lace filling worked into the four bars around a cut hardanger square
excerpt: The dove's eye is a lace filling used inside the open squares of hardanger embroidery. A loop of thread passes from bar to bar around the four sides of a cut square, twisting back on itself at each corner to form a central diamond or eye shape. It is worked as part of the bar sequence, pausing at the midpoint of each bar to catch the loop.
sourceNotes: Standard hardanger lace-filling technique; documented in Elsie Svennas, A Handbook of Hardanger Embroidery (1977) and widely in counted-thread needlework references. Formation details follow the standard four-bar loop method.

content.text: A dove's eye filling is made from a single looped thread that travels from the midpoint of one bar to the midpoints of the other three bars around the same open square, twisting the loop back on itself at each side. The result is a small diamond or eye shape suspended in the centre of the space. It must be worked during the bar-weaving sequence, not after all bars are finished, because the loop needs to catch through the midpoint of each bar as weaving reaches that point.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Perle cotton no 8; the same thread used for the woven bars

items.label: Fabric
items.value: 28-count evenweave linen or 22-count hardanger fabric, with kloster blocks complete and threads cut; woven bars begun

content.text: Begin weaving the first bar of the square as normal (see
). Stop when you reach the exact midpoint of this bar. The working thread is now at the centre of side one.

From the midpoint of bar one, carry the working thread across the open square to the midpoint of bar two (the bar on the adjacent side, going clockwise). Pass the needle through the midpoint of bar two from front to back, then loop the thread back on itself and pass it under the loop you just made, pulling gently to form a small twisted picot at that corner. This locks the loop at the midpoint of bar two.

Carry the thread across to the midpoint of bar three (the bar opposite bar one). Pass through and twist back as before to lock the loop at bar three. Then carry to bar four and repeat. After bar four, carry back to the midpoint of bar one and pass through the loop already there to close the eye. The four looped points now form a diamond in the centre of the square.

Return to bar one and complete the second half of its weaving to reach the far kloster block. Then weave bars two, three, and four from their starting edges to their far edges, picking up the dove's eye loop at each midpoint as you arrive there. The dove's eye loop passes through the eye without re-twisting.

items.symptom: The eye is off-centre or lopsided
items.cause: The working thread was not caught at the true midpoint of each bar
items.fix: Count the weaving passes before starting. On a standard bar of 4 threads, the midpoint falls after half the total weaving passes are complete. Mark it with a pin before starting if needed.

items.symptom: The loop slips out when finishing the remaining bar halves
items.cause: The twisted picot at each bar midpoint was not locked tightly enough, or the loop direction was inconsistent
items.fix: Pull each twisted picot firm before moving to the next bar. Keep the loop above the bar threads as you weave the second half, so the weaving passes pass beneath it and hold it in place.

items.symptom: The dove's eye looks tangled rather than forming a clear diamond
items.cause: The thread was carried in the wrong sequence, or the loop crossed over itself
items.fix: Work the four sides in strict clockwise order. After each carry, check that the thread lies cleanly above the open square without crossing previous loops before tightening.

content.text: The dove's eye is always used with
and cannot be added after bars are fully finished. The whole openwork structure depends on
